{"v": 1, "title": "Qwen Image 2.1 Cut Out + Remove", "subtitle": "Name a thing in your picture. You get it as a transparent PNG, and your picture with it gone.", "author": "AusBoss", "layout": "card", "accent": "", "body": "1. Load your image. You can crop it right there with the blue handles.
2. In **What to lift out**, name one thing, like "the dog" or "the woman on the left".
3. Optional: in **What to leave in its place**, say what should be there instead, like "an empty wooden bench". Leave it as it is to just take the thing out.
4. Press **Run**.

You get two pictures. **The cut-out** is the thing on a see-through background, saved as a PNG. **Your picture without it** has the thing taken out, along with its shadow and its reflection.

**Before and after** lets you slide between your picture and the result.

Both come out the same size, so they line up as two layers.

The rest of your picture is not repainted. Only the thing, a band around it, and what changed with it are pasted in.

If a piece of it stays, run it again. The seed changes each run.

**Consistency LoRA** (on): keeps your picture where it is while Qwen takes the thing out. Leave its row on, at 1.

**Speed LoRA** (optional): switch the Viggle Turbo row on and set **Steps** to 8. A run then takes about half the time.

Split Image with Alpha - Drop the see-through channel

nodes.title: Image Resize - Working size, about 1.5 megapixels
CLIP Text Encode - The name, for SAM 3
Mask Refine - Close holes, clean the edge
Mask Refine - A little past the edge
Image Composite Masked - Blank everything outside
Join Image with Alpha - The cut-out
Note
widgets_values: Your picture goes to about 1.5 megapixels, each side a multiple of 32. Both results come out at this size.

widgets_values_named.text: Your picture goes to about 1.5 megapixels, each side a multiple of 32. Both results come out at this size.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: SAM 3 reads the name you typed and marks where that thing is in your picture.

widgets_values_named.text: SAM 3 reads the name you typed and marks where that thing is in your picture.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: Small holes are closed, stray specks go, and the edge is softened by one pixel. A second copy reaches 8 pixels further out.

widgets_values_named.text: Small holes are closed, stray specks go, and the edge is softened by one pixel. A second copy reaches 8 pixels further out.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: Everything further out than that is blanked, so the file holds only the thing. Then the outside becomes see-through.

widgets_values_named.text: Everything further out than that is blanked, so the file holds only the thing. Then the outside becomes see-through.

nodes.title: Image RGB to YUV - How strong the change is
Threshold Mask - Count a change from 3 percent
Mask Refine - What changed, grown a little
Mask Refine - The thing and a band around it
Image Composite Masked - Paste only those areas
Note
widgets_values: Both pictures are blurred first, so film grain and fine detail do not count as a change.

widgets_values_named.text: Both pictures are blurred first, so film grain and fine detail do not count as a change.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: The blurred pictures are compared both ways, darker and lighter. A spot counts as changed from 3 percent, so faint leftovers go too.

widgets_values_named.text: The blurred pictures are compared both ways, darker and lighter. A spot counts as changed from 3 percent, so faint leftovers go too.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: What changed, and the thing with a band around it, each with a soft edge, then joined.

widgets_values_named.text: What changed, and the thing with a band around it, each with a soft edge, then joined.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: Only those areas are taken from Qwen's picture. Every other pixel is your own.
